title: Normalize token handoff and rename layer keys for tables & charts library
creator: Ava Martinez
description:
Goal: Reduce friction between design tokens and engineering consumption by normalizing token names, formalizing a layer-key naming convention, and cleaning up auto-layout constraints for table and chart components before next library publish. This ticket focuses on: 1) auditing current token usage in tables/charts (spacing, row height, legend swatches, axis labels), 2) renaming file layer keys to an agreed contract (component__part--state), 3) removing fragile auto-layout stacks that cause resizing regressions, and 4) producing a safe publish plan with migration notes for consumers.

Background: During partner onboarding we saw multiple regressions where front-end mappings failed because layer names differed between files and tokens had inconsistent semantic names (e.g., "table-row-gap" vs "row-spacing-md"). Chart legends and small density table variants often relied on nested manual spacing which prevents consistent responsive behavior. This causes teardown work for engineering and intermittent visual bugs in product.

Scope / Non-goals:
- In scope: Figma files under /Libraries/Components/Tables and /Libraries/Components/Charts, tokens referenced by those components, rename conventions, autolayout fixes for primary component variants, update library publish notes.
- Out of scope: button/token system-wide refactor, tokens used only by other libraries (e.g., forms) unless shared with tables/charts.

Deliverables:
- Canonical token mapping spreadsheet (TokenKey -> semantic usage -> suggested rename).
- A one-page style guide for layer-key naming: pattern "component__part--state" with examples.
- Updated Figma assets: tables and charts components with autolayout constraints normalized and layer keys renamed.
- Migration.md with breaking-change list and recommended CSS/React mapping for engineers.
- Merge-ready design PR and library publish checklist.

Acceptance criteria:
- All renamed tokens have a matching entry in the mapping spreadsheet and a migration note.
- Primary table/chart components (dense, default, expanded; legend, axis, tooltip) pass visual QA in Storybook snapshots produced by Eng (link in links).
- No autolayout regressions when resizing frame widths between 320px and 1440px in Figma tests.
- Publish notes added and the library can be published behind a gated rollout (canary teams).

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: Renaming tokens will break consumers. Mitigation: provide a compatibility table and keep old tokens as aliases in the tokens file for 2 weeks post-publish.
- Risk: Autolayout changes shift pixel positions for apps using absolute positioning. Mitigation: add a small migration PR for each affected product component with screenshots and suggested CSS adjustments.

Implementation plan (high-level):
1) 2025-02-10 to 2025-02-13 — Audit: run token extractor on files, collate usage, flag inconsistencies.
2) 2025-02-14 to 2025-02-16 — Proposal: draft layer-key naming doc, propose canonical token names, review with Eng and PM.
3) 2025-02-17 to 2025-02-19 — Apply renames and autolayout fixes in a separate Figma branch file; maintain old variants as deprecated hidden frames.
4) 2025-02-20 — Hand off mapping and migration.md to Eng, create design PR and publish notes.
5) 2025-02-24 to 2025-02-28 — Monitor canary usage, collect feedback, and revert any urgent regressions.

Notes on trade-offs:
- We prefer a semantically meaningful token naming convention (e.g., spacing.row-sm) over platform-specific names to future-proof cross-platform mapping, accepting an initial migration cost.
- Where autolayout fixes require restructuring nested frames, we'll keep a deprecated copy to allow engineering time to adapt rather than immediate deletion.

Acceptance sign-off: PM (Nora Patel), Eng lead (Diego Rivera), Design lead (Carmen Okafor).
